daily-grind - menu - guided.prompt: Update the navigation bar and seasonal favorite cards in index.html with an interactive menu component that lets users choose from a list of actions and options, including multi-level nested submenus for drink categories and order customizations. Order customizations include at least one on/off option and at least one pick-one option.

results.message: Each trigger is a button[type="button"] with aria-haspopup="menu", commandfor, command="toggle-popover", and no popovertarget or popovertargetaction
Menus are anchored to their triggers via CSS Anchor Positioning without per-menu CSS anchor rules, positioning top-level menus below and submenus beside with indented fallback
Menu items align their content across rows with fixed-size leading icon or check slot and trailing content at inline end, without subgrid
Each menu list has focusgroup="menu nomemory" on an element inside its popover, exposes role="menu" labeled by its trigger via aria-labelledby, and exposes role="menuitem" on command buttons

Separators between item groups are <hr> elements, checkable items are button[type="button"] with role="menuitemcheckbox" or "menuitemradio" (radios in named role="group") and aria-checked, Space toggles checkbox and keeps open, Enter toggles and closes, radios close on either key
Each popover is the immediate next sibling of its trigger, submenus are popover="auto" placed after trigger inside parent focusgroup without aria-details, and closed submenus are not inline

Focusing a submenu trigger previews its submenu and sets aria-expanded="true" without moving focus into the submenu, and moving focus to a sibling item closes that submenu and sets aria-expanded="false"

results.message: Inside an open menu, ArrowUp and ArrowDown move focus between enabled items, and Home and End move focus to first and last enabled item

Pressing ArrowRight on a submenu trigger opens the submenu and moves focus to its first enabled item, while pressing ArrowLeft in a submenu closes only that submenu and restores focus to its parent trigger
Pressing Escape closes only current menu level, sets trigger aria-expanded to "false", and restores focus to the trigger that opened it, including for nested submenus
Pressing Tab from a trigger or inside an open menu closes all open menus and leaves the menu system instead of stepping through every command

results.message: Activating a command item closes all open menu levels, restores focus to the root menu trigger, and never leaves focus inside hidden content
A submenu trigger only opens its submenu and never also runs a command; a default action is the first submenu item or a separate command item
Checked items render a visible check mark in the leading slot (::before content is not empty); unchecked items do not
At a 375 px viewport, an open submenu sits directly below its trigger item and its box does not intersect the trigger box
After a pointer activation of a command, focus returns to the root trigger without :focus-visible

devtools-times - local-network-access -.prompt: Add a developer diagnostics connection widget to The DevTools Times that lets readers connect from their browser to both a hardware test device on their private Wi-Fi LAN (such as 192.168.1.x) and a local companion CLI running on their own machine (127.0.0.1).

results.message: queries granular permission (local-network or loopback-network) via navigator.permissions.query() with fallback error handling
never queries the legacy local-network-access permission name via navigator.permissions.query()
specifies targetAddressSpace: local for local network requests and targetAddressSpace: loopback for loopback requests in fetch() or Request options
gates local network and loopback requests on explicit user interaction when permission state is prompt rather than firing unconditionally on page load
catches denied or failed local network and loopback requests and reveals error or remediation feedback in the UI

task - group-element-transitions - guide.prompt: Add an interactive coffee bean selection section to the Daily Grind homepage where users can add or remove items, using a group transition that smoothly animates items simultaneously between positions while maintaining page interactivity.

results.message: 1. Multiple elements on the page have a view-transition-class property set to the same value
2. Every element with a view-transition-class also has a unique view-transition-name
3. There are no repeated view-transition-name values
4. The stylesheet contains a ::view-transition-group rule targeting that class name
5. The animation-duration for the ::view-transition-group targeting that class is a time
6. The animation-timing-function for the ::view-transition-group targeting that class is non-linear (or default ease)
7. A prefers-reduced-motion rule sets the animation to none
8. New elements (entering) are transitioned using ::view-transition-new:only-child
9. Removed elements (exiting) are transitioned using ::view-transition-old:only-child
10. DOM updates that change the list are wrapped in a document.startViewTransition call
11. If document.startViewTransition is not defined, the DOM updates are made immediately
12. The Add button is interactive during the transition
13. The ::view-transition pseudo-element has pointer-events none
14. The view-transition-name on :root is set to none

task - full-session-analytics - guided.prompt: Implement Core Web Vitals monitoring on this site using the `web-vitals` JavaScript library. The page should send the Core Web Vitals data to a collection endpoint at `/path/to/analytics/endpoint`, and it should wait to send the data until the user closes the tab or navigates away, to make sure the metric values are finalized before collecting. Ensure telemetry is tracked reliably across the entire page visit without relying on legacy unload event listeners that break bfcache.

results.message: The fetchLater() API is invoked with a URL string and a DeferredRequestInit object
The fetchLater() API is the only API used for beacons (no direct fetch, sendBeacon, XMLHttpRequest, or new Image)
If a fetchLater() call throws a QuotaExceededError, it is properly handled with a try/catch
The fetchLater() polyfill is included in the bundle
Only a single beacon is sent, after the user leaves the page

task - forms - guided.prompt: Build an accessible, secure, and user-friendly multi-step registration form for the Daily Grind rewards program above the footer, following modern web form best practices for structure, labeling, input types, autofill, validation, and submission security.

results.message: The implementation MUST use a <form> element to wrap interactive controls
The <form> element MUST specify the "action" attribute
The <form> element MUST use method="POST" for sensitive data
Every form control MUST have a "name" attribute
The implementation MUST use semantic tags like <button type="submit">
The implementation MUST use <fieldset> and <legend> to group related controls
Submit buttons MUST use actionable language
Mutually exclusive options (1-5) MUST use radio buttons
Mutually exclusive options (6+) MUST NOT use radio buttons
Massive or dynamic sets (10+) MUST use <datalist>
Every input MUST be associated with a semantic <label>
Labels MUST be visually placed above form controls
Labels MUST be visible
Vertical margin between label and input MUST be less than margin between groups
Implementation MUST use aria-describedby
The "lang" attribute MUST be defined on the <html> element
Required fields MUST have native validation and indicators
Implementation MUST use autocomplete
Implementation MUST NOT use type="number" for zip/cc
Input font-size MUST be at least 16px
Tap targets MUST be at least 48px
Focus outlines MUST NOT be disabled
Validation MUST NOT show on input
Validation MUST show on blur
Implementation MUST provide password toggle
Implementation MUST include CSRF token
Implementation MUST NOT use inline JavaScript
Implementation MUST use single field for names
Implementation MUST display progress
The password toggle button must expose state via aria-pressed and link warning via aria-describedby
The implementation must not use <section> elements as individual form field layout containers

daily-grind - swipe-to-reveal - unguided.prompt: Update the Seasonal Favorites cards in index.html so that swiping horizontally on a drink item reveals contextual action buttons for that drink without automatically executing an action.

results.message: Horizontal swipe-to-reveal container is a horizontal scroll container configured with mandatory CSS Scroll Snap and no manual JS gesture listeners
Foreground content element sets scroll-snap-align: start, scroll-initial-target: nearest, and an opaque background, while trailing panels snap to end
Outer horizontal swipe-to-reveal container sets overscroll-behavior: chain in CSS without contain or none
Revealed action controls or side-menu items are focusable DOM elements inside the swipe-to-reveal container
Keyboard focus (focusin paired with :focus-visible) scrolls the foreground content element back to inline start

task - swipe-to-remove - unguided.prompt: can you add a shopping cart section underneath the seasonal favorites on our menu page? list items like Maple Oat Latte, Dark Roast Espresso, and Cold Brew, and implement a swipe-to-remove gesture on each item in the list. please use our team's naming convention: the list should be a ul with class 'SwipeableList', and each item a li with class 'SwipeableList-item' (adding 'is-initialized' once initialized). inside each item, put a 'SwipeableList-track' container and a 'SwipeableList-content' element. when a user swipes past a certain point, the item should show an action color and smoothly collapse down in height to remove it from the page.

results.message: Track has scroll-snap-type x mandatory
Track has overscroll-behavior-x none
Track hides its scrollbar with scrollbar-width none
Track spacers have scroll-snap-align set to be valid snap targets
Content element has scroll-snap-align set
Content element has an opaque background to hide action behind it
scroll-initial-target nearest is gated behind initialization class
Swipe detector IntersectionObserver is rooted at the track
Swipe detector has low commit and high activate thresholds
Updates data-swipe-direction attribute during swipe
Toggles is-activating class during swipe before commit
Triggers row collapse animation when swiped past commit threshold
Does not drive the swipe with manual pointermove transform updates
MutationObserver wires up dynamically added list items
scroll-initial-target fallback scrolls track programmatically when CSS.supports is false
ResizeObserver is attached to track when fallback is active
ResizeObserver is NOT attached to track when scroll-initial-target is supported
Safari scroll-latching workaround defers item removal and sets inert
Non-Safari browsers remove the item immediately after collapse
Uses WAAPI animations to collapse row height and translate content
Projects focus affordance onto content element when track has focus

task - support-global-calendar-systems -.prompt: Add a world calendar converter section below Seasonal Favorites on the homepage where visitors can pick a date and see it displayed in cards for the Islamic (inside an element with id="islamic-date"), Hebrew, and Japanese calendars, showing each calendar's localized date (including era names for Japanese), converted year, numeric month, and month code, total months in that calendar year, whether the selected date is in the past, today, or future ("Past", "Future", or "Today"), and a breakdown of the months in that calendar year with each month's code and day count.

results.message: The implementation feature-detects Temporal and assigns the loaded polyfill to `globalThis.Temporal`.

task - search-hidden-content - unguided.prompt: Add mutually exclusive wholesale and catering tabs with class "wholesale-tab" whose hidden content remains discoverable via browser search, plus a reveal coupon button that displays a discount panel with id "coupon-panel" whose contents are also searchable before disclosure.

results.message: The wholesale-tab elements use the <details> element
The <details> mutually exclusive regions share a name attribute
The coupon-panel uses the hidden="until-found" attribute
The coupon-panel does not have display: none or visibility: hidden
The coupon-panel does not hide sensitive information
State is synchronized using a beforematch event listener
Implementation includes explicit fallback strategy with feature detection

task - scrollytelling - unguided.prompt: Add a scrollytelling section with text steps (each a `section` element) inside container "#tracked" and visual elements (each a `section` element) inside container "#animated" that animate based on the scroll position of the corresponding text sections across different DOM branches.

results.message: Named view-timelines are defined on tracked elements.
timeline-scope is used on a common ancestor to make named timelines accessible.
Target elements use animation-timeline linked to the named timelines.
animation-range controls animation timing relative to the tracked elements.
The implementation includes feature detection using @supports for scroll-driven animations.
The implementation respects user preferences for reduced motion using @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).

daily-grind - scrollspy - unguided.prompt: Convert the Daily Grind sticky navigation bar links (Menu, Locations, Rewards, and My Account) into in-page section anchors with corresponding content sections on the homepage, and highlight whichever section is currently visible in the navigation bar as the user scrolls.

results.message: Navigation links use fragment identifiers that match the unique IDs of their target content sections
The navigation container has scroll-target-group: auto applied to enable native browser tracking
Navigation links use the :target-current pseudo-class combined with the fallback selector inside :is()
The aria-current state is synchronized with the visible section when scrolling stops using a scrollend event listener
The link corresponding to the section currently in view is visually highlighted with a color change and contrast or a non-color indicator
The aria-current attribute is set to "true" on the navigation link corresponding to the visible section and "false" on all other links
When scroll-target-group: auto is not supported, an IntersectionObserver fallback toggles a fallback active class on the active navigation link

5. The animation-duration for the ::view-transition-group targeting that class is a time
6. The animation-timing-function for the ::view-transition-group targeting that class is non-linear (or default ease)

8. New elements (entering) are transitioned using ::view-transition-new:only-child
9. Removed elements (exiting) are transitioned using ::view-transition-old:only-child

13. The ::view-transition pseudo-element has pointer-events none
14. The view-transition-name on :root is set to none

task - forms - unguided.prompt: Build an accessible, secure, and user-friendly multi-step registration form for the Daily Grind rewards program above the footer, following modern web form best practices for structure, labeling, input types, autofill, validation, and submission security.

results.message: The implementation MUST use a <form> element to wrap interactive controls
The <form> element MUST specify the "action" attribute
The <form> element MUST use method="POST" for sensitive data
Every form control MUST have a "name" attribute
The implementation MUST use semantic tags like <button type="submit">
The implementation MUST use <fieldset> and <legend> to group related controls
Submit buttons MUST use actionable language
Mutually exclusive options (1-5) MUST use radio buttons
Mutually exclusive options (6+) MUST NOT use radio buttons
Massive or dynamic sets (10+) MUST use <datalist>
Every input MUST be associated with a semantic <label>
Labels MUST be visually placed above form controls
Labels MUST be visible
Vertical margin between label and input MUST be less than margin between groups
Implementation MUST use aria-describedby
The "lang" attribute MUST be defined on the <html> element
Required fields MUST have native validation and indicators
Implementation MUST use autocomplete
Implementation MUST NOT use type="number" for zip/cc
Input font-size MUST be at least 16px
Tap targets MUST be at least 48px
Focus outlines MUST NOT be disabled
Validation MUST NOT show on input
Validation MUST show on blur
Implementation MUST provide password toggle
Implementation MUST include CSRF token
Implementation MUST NOT use inline JavaScript
Implementation MUST use single field for names
Implementation MUST display progress
The password toggle button must expose state via aria-pressed and link warning via aria-describedby
The implementation must not use <section> elements as individual form field layout containers

The implementation uses Temporal.ZonedDateTime as the primary type for scheduling and managing events
The implementation does not use Temporal.PlainDateTime for scheduling global events
The implementation uses disambiguation: reject option in Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from() or toZonedDateTime() for conflict detection

The implementation does not attempt to modify Temporal instances directly as they are immutable
The implementation displays correct DST-aware converted time for Tokyo

daily-grind - contrast-color - unguided.prompt: Update the navigation bar, action buttons, and footer on the Daily Grind homepage so their text colors automatically adapt to remain readable with high contrast whenever the primary or secondary theme background colors are changed dynamically in the styles.

results.message: If the browser does not support contrast-color(), the themed element still has a readable fallback text color (not the browser default)

For variable background colors in browsers that do not support contrast-color(), the themed element uses Relative Color Syntax (oklch(from ...)), a text-shadow, a -webkit-text-stroke with paint-order: stroke fill, a translucent background overlay, or an SVG filter
The contrast-color() function is not used to define the background-color property of any element
The text color of themed elements computes to either rgb(0, 0, 0) or rgb(255, 255, 255) when a background color is applied
